subject.title: Support for Telegram bot-to-bot and guest-bot modes (Telegram May-7 2026 release)

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a staged Telegram-owned design—first explicit Guest Mode with isolated sessions, then safe bot-to-bot admission and loop protection—while routing multi-agent delegation semantics through plugins rather than core?
rationale: The work adds public configuration, new transport authorization semantics, session identity, outbound behavior, and a potential orchestration model; source evidence and the open partial PR cannot choose the permanent product boundary.

options.title: Sponsor staged Telegram support
options.body: Approve a narrow Guest Mode path and a separately reviewed opt-in peer-bot policy with shared loop protection, while keeping delegation protocols out of core by default.

options.title: Limit scope to Guest Mode
options.body: Accept only the isolated Guest Mode use case and explicitly reject or defer bot-to-bot peer routing until a plugin demonstrates a missing core extension API.

options.title: Keep all new modes external
options.body: Require a plugin-owned implementation for Guest Mode and bot-to-bot workflows unless maintainers identify a core Telegram API gap that cannot be expressed through current seams.

recommendation.title: Sponsor staged Telegram support
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow Guest Mode path and a separately reviewed opt-in peer-bot policy with shared loop protection, while keeping delegation protocols out of core by default.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Telegram architecture/configuration and loop-protection history makes this the strongest available routing candidate.
